rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Material decrease in required minimum umbrella/excess liability insurance limit from $5M to $2M.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 9 atomic changes. Removal of the $5,000 monthly floor lowers the minimum local advertising obligation for low-revenue parks. Mandatory opening deadline shortened from 15 months to 12 months, increasing time pressure on the franchisee.

2 atomic changes. Changes the basis of territory sizing from geography/zip codes to a radius-based system of 3-5 miles, altering the scope of territorial exclusivity. Introduces a new carve-out that waives the minimum population requirement when the maximum radius is reached, altering territory qualification.
1 atomic change. Trademark status changed from pending application to registered, a material legal status change disclosed in Item 13.

4 atomic changes. Material change in the level of detail and naming of income statement metrics, including new disaggregated expense lines and percentages. Material change in disclosure method: from a single actual income statement to a low/high/average summary.

2 atomic changes. The 2025 FDD revises previously reported franchised outlet counts for 2022 and 2023 in both systemwide and state-level tables, a material change to disclosed outlet information. Adding partial-year 2025 outlet data through June 13 is a clear disclosure-method and coverage change beyond a pure year roll.
1 atomic change. New disclosure of unaudited interim financial statements with an explicit audit disclaimer changes the financial information available to prospective franchisees.
5 atomic changes. Material increase in the disclosed lower bound of the 16-foot container price range. Material change in the disclosed lower bound of the 20-foot container price range.
1 atomic change. Replaces expected fund establishment in 2023-2024 with a right to establish at any time, changing the trigger for a conditional monthly fee.
4 atomic changes. Material increase in the fixed estimated cost of the required Lift System. Material increase in the disclosed estimated additional container inventory range.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New optional insurance-supplier rebate arrangement creates a disclosed franchisor revenue stream not present in the prior year.

2 atomic changes. Reported franchised outlet stock increased from 2 to 7 at year-end, a clear operational change. Projected openings are now disclosed by state rather than as an aggregate total, a disclosure-method change.
1 atomic change. Removal of a disclosure identifying the owner and applicant of the marks is a clear disclosure-method change with limited direct economic effect.

2 atomic changes. The audited statement changed from a single balance-sheet date to a period from inception through fiscal year end, altering the disclosed reporting coverage. Disclosed audited statement type broadened from a balance sheet to audited financial statements, changing the Item 21 disclosure content.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. A new contractual condition was introduced for franchisees who choose to build their own Store. The disclosed target size range for Shops changed its upper bound from 600 to 900 square feet.
1 atomic change. A new mandatory Franchisee Build Addendum was introduced for franchisee-built stores, creating a new contractual obligation.

4 atomic changes. Accounting and backoffice software fee changed from not charged to estimated $175 per month per store. Network/Internet/telephone support fee estimate increased from $250 to $275 per month per store.
20 atomic changes. Per-person additional training cost for Shop changed in both endpoints. Per-person additional training cost for Store increased.
1 atomic change. Introduction of a new Franchisee Build Addendum into the Item 9 obligation cross-reference table is a structural change to the franchise agreement documents.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Shift of training material costs to franchisee for opening inventory items is a material cost reallocation. Increase in estimated gift card vendor initial cost from $50 to $135.
1 atomic change. Clear operational change in how the territory radius is determined, adding a new reference to the Search Area Addendum and Approved Site selection.
8 atomic changes. Cost of Sales definition now explicitly includes delivery charges, a material calculation-method change. Cost of Sales disclosure universe changed from 118 to 106 franchised stores.
1 atomic change. New contract exhibit added to the Item 22 contracts list; operational/contract change with unknown terms.

2 atomic changes. Royalty fee changed from a fixed monthly amount to a percentage-of-revenue formula with a minimum, fundamentally restructuring the fee. New 8% royalty on Gross Collected Revenues introduces a material revenue-based fee component.
1 atomic change. The payee for equipment/computer/software purchases changes from suppliers only to suppliers and the franchisor, altering the payment flow without changing the amount.
1 atomic change. Removal of the franchisor's discretionary financing offer materially changes franchisee access to capital and associated obligations.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Fee base changed, potentially affecting the fee amount.
1 atomic change. New contractual provision grants the franchisor ownership of all franchisee-developed IP, a material economic-condition change.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. A required contractual instrument for Substitute Manager delegation changes from a Noncompetition Agreement to a Brand Protection Agreement. The separately named agreement required of owners and spouses changes from a Noncompetition Agreement to a Franchise Owner Agreement.

5 atomic changes. Removal of the entire expense and net income disclosure fundamentally restructures the Item 19 representation. Introduction of a new performance metric materially expands the disclosure.
1 atomic change. The disclosed contract form at Attachment C changed names; substantive equivalence is unverified.
1 atomic change. The Item 4 content changed from a no-disclosure-required statement to a substantive bankruptcy-history disclosure, a clear disclosure-method/content change.

4 atomic changes. The Item 9 table dropped its separate Area Development Agreement cross-reference column, a disclosure-method restructuring. The set of other disclosure items cross-referenced for the pre-opening purchases obligation changed (Item 5 added), a disclosure-method update.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. Changes the non-compete covenant from a request-triggered obligation to a mandatory agreement with an express one-year post-termination prohibition. Introduces mandatory employment of five specified positions, a material operational and cost obligation.

4 atomic changes. The FPR shifts from single-store data to group aggregate statistics, a fundamental disclosure-method change. The FPR outlet universe and ownership type changed from a single affiliate store to all franchisee-owned centers, fundamentally restructuring the representation.

2 atomic changes. The FDD changes its disclosure of franchisee confidentiality restrictions from 'in some instances' to 'no franchisee has signed' in the last three fiscal years. The geographic scope of franchised outlets expanded from a single state to multiple states, a clear operational change.

2 atomic changes. The disclosure of audited financial statements expanded from two fiscal years to three fiscal years, a material change in the information provided to prospective franchisees. The removal of the limitation statement changes the disclosed eligibility status and the scope of financial statements provided, a material disclosure change.
7 atomic changes. A significant area development agreement was removed from the attached contracts. A contract containing guarantee and indemnification obligations was removed.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 20 atomic changes. Franchisor's optional repurchase right became a mandatory purchase obligation, fundamentally restructuring the post-termination asset arrangement. Dispute resolution initial step changed from JAMS mediation to an in-person executive meeting with a five-business-day deadline.

8 atomic changes. Historical company-owned outlet end count for 2013 changed from 2 to 0 between FDD versions. Historical company-owned outlet start count for 2014 changed from 2 to 0 between FDD versions.
1 atomic change. Item 21 discloses an unaudited profit and loss statement for a longer interim period (10 months vs 6 months), a disclosure coverage change.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New optional offering structure allowing simultaneous purchase of multiple franchises under a development schedule. Material disclosure change from no parent to a named parent company.
1 atomic change. The veteran discount percentage was reduced from 15% to 10%, increasing the net initial fee for eligible veteran franchisees.

6 atomic changes. Daily training fee rate increased from $600 to $750 per day, a material fee increase. Hourly training fee rate increased from $100 to $125 per hour per trainer, a material fee increase.

3 atomic changes. Same EarthWise Initial Opening Inventory row shows the disclosed cost range revised from $50,000-$65,000 to $70,000-$90,000. Same EarthWise FFE row shows the disclosed cost range high end revised from $105,000 to $115,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 11 atomic changes. Adds specific, separate auto liability limits, increasing required coverage. Adds a 24-month minimum duration for business interruption coverage.

10 atomic changes. Removal of a 70% down-payment financing option is a material fee-structure change. Removal of a termination right tied to financing default is a material control/enforcement change.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Development schedule restructured from opening deadlines to lease-signing deadlines with different intervals. New contractual deadline to open within 8 months of signing a lease, with termination for non-compliance.

2 atomic changes. Adds a clear operational prerequisite for franchisee to obtain formal written approval before signing a lease, increasing franchisor control over location selection. Introduces a new coordination and oversight mechanism for local customer issues involving multiple franchisees, giving franchisor a right to reasonable direction.

1 atomic change. The franchisor's contractual obligation to indemnify and defend the franchisee against trademark claims was replaced by a discretionary right with no obligation, materially increasing franchisee risk and cost exposure.

2 atomic changes. Introduced a new franchisor right to change or discontinue IP subject matter and a corresponding franchisee obligation to modify or discontinue use at the franchisee's sole expense. Expanded the enumerated scope of trade secrets and changed the characterization from 'such processes' to 'some of such processes and information'.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Material change expanding the post-termination non-compete geographic scope from outlets to outlets or territories. Operational timing change reducing the required minimum renewal notice from 6 to 3 months.

11 atomic changes. The disclosed outlet population changed materially from including company-owned stores to franchisee-owned only. A new mobile grooming van scenario with distinct revenue and expense assumptions was added to the pro forma.

9 atomic changes. The disclosed attribution of 2023 ceased-operations outlets to the Large Franchisee was restated from 16 to 10, with the denominator also changed from 18 to 14. Prior-year reported company-owned outlet count at start of 2022 was restated from 1 to 2.

3 atomic changes. New mandatory payment obligation up to $40,000 for subleased premises is a material fee change. New disclosure of a cost range for affiliate purchases is a small but substantive operational change.
1 atomic change. Reconciliation condition added; debit trigger now tied to due date.

3 atomic changes. Removal of a disclosed discretionary fee changes the potential economic burden on the franchisee. Removal of a conditional lease guarantee changes the disclosed availability of franchisor credit support.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Adds explicit franchisee cost obligation for equipment and installation. Adds explicit franchisee cost obligation for inventory and supplies.

2 atomic changes. Explicitly adds franchisor discretion to deny relocation consent, a clear change in the disclosure of contractual control. Adds a broader statement that no additional franchise rights exist under the Franchise Agreement, going beyond the prior Development Area/contiguous-territory scope.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Adds a new default trigger: termination of a unit Franchise Agreement due to Developer default now constitutes a default under the Area Development Agreement. Addition of a carve-out to the integration clause that preserves reliance on FDD representations.
1 atomic change. Clear change in disclosure content from an exhibit listing trademark-specific franchisee organizations to an explicit statement that none exist.
1 atomic change. The disclosed estimated insurance range decreased at both bounds in the same Item 7 row; this is a clear numeric disclosure change.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Changes the required kickoff marketing campaign format from a breakfast/lunch presentation to a Leadership Luncheon or Portfolio Program. Adds an explicit successful-completion-to-satisfaction condition to the timing of Initial Training before opening.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Addition of 'and subject to applicable state law' to the choice-of-law clause is a clear legal-scope change, not administrative.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Removal of a disclosed conversion franchise program is a clear operational/offering change with economic meaning. A new regulatory finding and reclassification from 'Licensed Stores' to 'USA Franchised Stores' materially changes the disclosed legal status of prior licensees.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Removes the conversion addendum exception to the telephone listing assignment consent condition; now all stores must deliver it. Newly discloses a specific $3,000 initial training fee for additional attendees, replacing an unspecified 'then required' fee.
1 atomic change. Removal of a franchisor discretionary statement about retaining protected areas upon a Conversion Addendum constitutes a material change in territorial discretion/control.
1 atomic change. Removal of a contractual exception granting converting franchisees ownership of pre-existing customer lists shifts control of customer data to the franchisor.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Removal of the disclosed carve-out for conversion franchises from the post-term competitive restrictions changes the scope of a significant non-compete obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Addition of a conditional exception to post-termination non-compete obligations when the franchise is mutually terminated due to the affiliate license ending materially narrows those obligations.
1 atomic change. The franchisor's disclosed policy regarding offering franchises to licensed stores changed from a conditional may-offer to a definite no-offer.
1 atomic change. A pending litigation disclosure was removed from the Item 3 disclosure, changing the disclosed litigation profile.
6 atomic changes. The disclosed annual website access fee per person increased by $25. Disclosed initial franchise fee for Inexperienced Travel Agents increased by $500.
7 atomic changes. The per-person annual Access Fee increased from $60 to $85. The per-associate administrative fee increased from $50 to $75.
1 atomic change. Initial franchise fee for Inexperienced Travel Agents increased by $500, a direct increase in an upfront required fee.
1 atomic change. The required down payment for franchisor financing of the initial franchise fee increased by $500.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Material increase in an annual per-person technology access fee charged to franchisees. New explicit numeric minimum internet speed requirement represents a measurable operational change.
1 atomic change. The revenue metric underlying the franchisor's termination threshold changes from 'Gross' to 'Departed' Commissionable Revenues, altering the condition that can trigger termination.

3 atomic changes. New Principal Register service mark registration disclosed in 2018 FDD, changing the trademark portfolio and legal protection available to the franchise system. Removal of explicit risk disclosure that trademarks lacked Principal Register benefits and that a challenge could increase expenses; a disclosure-method change.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. The post-termination non-compete changed from prohibiting only offering/selling/promoting/marketing Cruise and Travel Products to prohibiting any interest, employment, or engagement in the cruise/travel business with a Competing Business, materially broadening the restraint. The contractual revenue metric used to trigger a non-curable cause default changed from 'Annual Gross Commissionable Revenues' to 'Annual Departed Commissionable Revenues' while the dollar thresholds stayed the same.
1 atomic change. Change from explicit no FPR to a full financial performance representation with historical sales data constitutes a fundamental change in Item 19 disclosure.

1 atomic change. Disclosure method for current franchisee contact information in Exhibit C changed from business address to city/state and explicitly excludes home address; score 3 for a clear disclosure-method change.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 10 atomic changes. The entire Item 1 disclosure shifts from the three L&L brands to the MIXPLATE system as the subject of the FDD, a fundamental restructuring of the disclosed offering. MIXPLATE changed from a planned franchise to an actually offered franchise, a material change in the franchise opportunity.
1 atomic change. The franchise is granted under a different brand/format (L&L vs MIXPLATE), changing the core subject of the franchise grant.

16 atomic changes. Continuing franchise fee rate changes from flat 4% for 15 years to 4% for first 5 years and 5% for last 5 years, a material fee schedule change. Design review fee increases from $2,000 to $5,000, a material fee increase.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 14 atomic changes. New uncapped cost obligation for franchisee when Operations Manual changes are implemented. New potential franchisee cost obligation for laboratory testing of supplier samples.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 19 atomic changes. Adds explicit disclaimers of proportionality obligation and fiduciary duty, strengthening franchisor discretion. Expands advertising approval from individual advertisements to media-level consent and social media control.

4 atomic changes. Prohibits franchisee independent internet marketing and e-commerce, reversing prior permission. Expands franchisor's ability to place competing outlets from close proximity to any location.

7 atomic changes. Expanded franchisor right to change marks and imposed cost-bearing and liability waiver on franchisee; material change. The system under which the marks may be used changed from L & L to MIXPLATE, a material change in the franchise brand and authorized product scope.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 15 atomic changes. The purchase option price formula is modified to include the lower of stated formula or proposed sale price. Initial term reduced from 15 to 10 years, a material reduction in the franchisee's contractual tenure.

2 atomic changes. Removal of all financial performance representations constitutes fundamental restructuring of Item 19. Removal of a disclosure obligation that provided underlying sales data upon request.

2 atomic changes. The Item 20 disclosure scope changed from the L&L Hawaiian Barbecue system to the newly introduced MIXPLATE system, fundamentally restructuring the outlet reporting. Outlet reporting coverage narrowed from multiple states and international locations to California only, reducing geographic scope of Item 20 disclosures.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. 2023 FDD adds an optional cold plunge service option; clear scope/operational change but not a fee or obligation change.

6 atomic changes. Removal of a disclosed price discount increases the effective fee for the affected franchise purchase scenario. Material increase in a contractual initial franchise fee for third and additional simultaneous franchises.

3 atomic changes. The monthly local advertising obligation changed from a pure percentage formula to a greater-of-floor-and-percentage formula. The local marketing obligation now includes a $1,000 monthly minimum in addition to the percentage.
14 atomic changes. High-end build-out estimate increased from $225,000/$250,000 to $290,000. Computer system estimate decreased and was renamed Business Management System with mandated POS.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Floatation service offering changed from unconditional to conditional 'in some cases'. Disclosure changed from named approved suppliers to unnamed 'designated supplier' references.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. New $1,000 monthly floor on local advertising spend is a material financial obligation. Training fee increased from $4,000 to $7,500, a material financial change.

3 atomic changes. Explicit sole-discretion designation materially increases franchisor control over the territory. Relocation consent now explicitly rests on franchisor sole discretion and adds general non-exclusive consent criteria.
3 atomic changes. Newly disclosed material USPTO determination (refusal) changes trademark risk profile. Imposes a new financial obligation on franchisee for franchisor-initiated mark modifications.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The enumerated authorized service types changed from generic sauna and floatation to infrared sauna plus conditional floatation/cold plunge, altering the franchisee's permitted scope of operations.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Addition of a disclosure row stating the governing law (Tennessee, subject to state law) that was absent from the prior year's Item 17 table.

9 atomic changes. The disclosed bottom-line metric name and definition changed, altering the meaning of the performance representation. New percentage-of-revenue metrics add independently measurable performance disclosures.

4 atomic changes. Number of signed franchise agreements not yet opened rose from 0 to 8, a clear operational expectation change. Disclosure method changed from aggregate-only to state-level breakdown in the same table.
1 atomic change. The disclosed financial statement period/date changed from February 28, 2022 to September 30, 2022, a clear timing change.
1 atomic change. Staffing software license fee minimum annual amount decreased from $3,000 to $1,200, a material reduction in the disclosed lower bound.

2 atomic changes. The referral fee was previously uncapped and type-dependent; 2019 adds an explicit $1,000 cap on the fee the franchisor can receive, a material fee-term change. The 2019 item names a specific third-party lender, Benetrends, Inc., as currently providing financing, a new disclosure of a financing source.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Mandatory initial training's on-the-job hours increased from zero to 1-25 hours across many courses, materially expanding the disclosed training program. The lower bound of the disclosed initial computer system cost estimate decreased from $2,800 to $2,500 while the upper bound stayed at $5,000.

5 atomic changes. Introduction of a new financial performance representation for franchisees open for one fiscal year, materially expanding the types of performance disclosures. The disclosure of the sample's inclusion/exclusion criteria changed from no explicit exclusions to a detailed exclusion statement.
1 atomic change. Royalty fee structure changed from a tiered 4%/5%/6% schedule to a flat 5% rate, a material change in ongoing royalty obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New contractual obligation requiring franchisee participation in franchisor-designated social media programs; material control/obligation change.
